text: When an AI agent buys something for you, and the purchase is disputed, nobody can show what the agent was actually allowed to do. Agent Flight Recorder is that record.
First, a person signs a mandate: a budget, a per-order cap, named merchants, and an expiry. It is cryptographically signed, so it cannot be quietly edited later.

The agent proposes a purchase. Plain deterministic code, with no A I in the enforcement path, checks it before any PayPal order exists. This one is within the mandate, so a PayPal sandbox order is created and the step is logged.

Now a real A I model takes over the shopping. It is a small open model running locally, and the cheap shoe's listing is poisoned with hidden instructions. It takes the bait and proposes a two hundred forty-nine dollar shoe. The guard denies it, and PayPal is never called.
Over the per-order cap? Denied, with the exact rule that failed.
Above the approval threshold, the person is asked. Approval re-runs the guard, so a human yes can never override a hard rule.
Every step goes into an append-only log, where each event contains the hash of the one before it.
The log's head hash can be stamped by an independent timestamp authority, so a third party's signature pins everything before it.
For a dispute, the signed mandate and the full log become an evidence bundle that anyone can verify offline: the signature, every hash, and the timestamp.
Now someone edits one event directly in the database. Verification fails, and points at the exact event. This is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: events after the latest timestamp are not pinned.

The results are measured. Twenty-seven of twenty-seven red-team attacks blocked. A real local A I model strayed outside its mandate in fifteen of twenty-four live runs, and the guard denied every one. Two hundred nine of two hundred nine bundle edits detected. The honest limits: dispute submission is built to PayPal's API, but only tested against a fake, not yet on a live sandbox dispute. Sandbox only, built with A I assistance. The code is on GitHub.
